toolUseResult.originalFile:
# ForgeMark

**A concurrent git push/clone throughput benchmark for any smart-HTTP git forge.**

ForgeMark measures **sustained push or clone throughput and per-operation
latency** the way an agent fleet hits a forge: many concurrent writers, readers,
or mixed sessions. It drives **real git operations** through
[`go-git`](https://github.com/go-git/go-git) (packfile build + ref update for
pushes, upload-pack for clones), so it exercises the forge paths directly — not
a synthetic HTTP approximation.

It works against **any smart-HTTP git host** — GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket,
self-hosted, GitHub Enterprise Server, github.com, and
[Entire](https://github.com/entireio). There's no target flag: the forge is
inferred from `-remote` (and, for Entire, from the auth flags you supply).

> **Only run ForgeMark against infrastructure you own or are explicitly
> authorized to load-test.** A tight push loop is abusive traffic to a host that
> hasn't agreed to it.

## Install

```bash
go install github.com/entireio/forgemark/cmd/forgemark@latest
```

## What it measures

Per concurrency level it reports successful operations/sec,
p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max latency, and CAS-failure / error counts where they apply.
Results print as a table and are written to `results/forgemark-<id>.json` for
charting.

### Strategies

| `-strategy` | shape | what it tells you |
|---|---|---|
| `branch` (default) | N agents, **one repo**, each pushes its own branch | **Headline single-repo number.** No client-side contention (each agent owns its ref), so it isolates the server's per-repo ref-update path. |
| `repo` | N agents spread across **M repos** (`-repo-count`), own branches | Horizontal-scale ceiling — distinct repos serialize independently, so this should scale where `branch` saturates. |
| `clone` | N agents, **one repo**, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → discard → repeat | Read-side ceiling: how many concurrent shallow clones/sec the forge sustains, without write load. |
| `session` | N agents, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → commit+push `-session-commits` checkpoints to a fresh ephemeral branch → abandon → repeat | Realistic agent lifecycle: interleaves **read load (clone) with write load (push)** on one repo. Reports clone and push latencies separately. |

## Usage

Two steps: **set up the target repos**, then **run**.

### 1. Set up targets

ForgeMark does not create repos — it pushes to ones you provide. Create them on
your forge and make sure your credential can push:

- **`branch`** needs **one empty repo**.
- **`repo`** needs **M empty repos**.
- **`clone`** and **`session`** need a repo with a **base branch that has
  content** to clone. An empty repo degrades to a no-read orphan, so a read-side
  run against an unseeded repo isn't measuring what you think — push a base
  branch first.

Per forge, roughly:

```bash
# GitHub (needs the gh CLI): a throwaway private repo
gh repo create you/forgemark-target --private
# for clone/session runs, give it content:
#   git clone … && git commit --allow-empty -m base && git push

# GitLab / Gitea / self-hosted: create an empty repo in the UI or via the
# forge's API, ensure your token/user can push, and (for clone/session) push a
# base branch with at least one commit.
```

### 2. Run

Most forges just need a token. Point `-remote` at the host and supply the token
via `-token-file` (a file, or `-` for stdin):

```bash
FORGE="-remote https://git.example.com"

# Headline: single-repo throughput, sweep concurrency
# (-token-file reads a file; use "-" to pipe the token in on stdin instead)
forgemark $FORGE -token-file ~/.forge-token \
  -repos org/repo -concurrency 1,8,32 -duration 2m

# Spread across 16 repos (horizontal scale)
forgemark $FORGE -token-file ~/.forge-token -strategy repo \
  -repo-pattern "org/bench-{n}" -repo-count 16 -concurrency 32,128 -duration 2m

# Clone: read-side throughput, discard each in-memory clone (needs a seeded base branch)
forgemark $FORGE -token-file ~/.forge-token -repos org/repo \
  -strategy clone -clone-depth 1 -concurrency 8,32 -duration 2m

# Session: clone + push 5 checkpoints, abandon, repeat (needs a seeded base branch)
forgemark $FORGE -token-file ~/.forge-token -repos org/repo \
  -strategy session -session-commits 5 -clone-depth 1 -concurrency 8,32
```

The push URL is `<-remote>/<repo>` — the `-repos` value is appended **verbatim**
(ForgeMark does no path rewriting), so include a `.git` suffix if your forge
needs it. The token is used as the basic-auth password with a conventional
username (`-user` to override); most forges accept a PAT this way. The secret
comes from `-token-file` or the `ACCESS_TOKEN` env var — never a CLI flag, so it
can't leak via `ps` or shell history. Entire needs a couple of extra flags — see
below.

## Entire

Entire needs two extra flags — `-token-url` and `-jurisdiction`. Auth is a
single short-lived **jurisdiction identity token**: ForgeMark exchanges your
subject token for it (RFC 8693) and refreshes it, so one token authorizes every
repo you can reach. Pass the subject token as `-token-file`/`ACCESS_TOKEN`:

```bash
forgemark -remote https://aws-us-east-2.entire.io \
  -token-url    https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token \
  -jurisdiction https://us.entire.io \
  -token-file   ~/.entire-subject-token \
  -repos your/repo -concurrency 1,8,32,128 -duration 2m
```

`-repos` is appended verbatim — ForgeMark does no path rewriting, so pass the
full repo path exactly as your Entire deployment expects it. The exact form is
deployment-specific — see the runbook.

Deployment-specific setup (obtaining the subject token, target provisioning) and
methodology notes live in Entire's own runbook.

## github.com

github.com is just a generic remote — point `-remote` at it with a PAT
(needs **contents: write**):

```bash
gh repo create you/forgemark-throwaway --private
gh auth token | forgemark -remote https://github.com -token-file - \
  -repos you/forgemark-throwaway -concurrency 1,4 -duration 30s
```

**Keep concurrency low.** github.com applies secondary rate limits and abuse
detection to high-volume content writes; a tight push loop at high concurrency
will get throttled or blocked, and high-volume automated load testing of
github.com isn't sanctioned by their acceptable-use policy. ForgeMark detects a
`github.com` remote and warns above concurrency 16. For a higher-volume
comparison, point `-remote` at a **GitHub Enterprise Server** you control.

## Key flags

| flag | default | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `-remote` | — | base URL of the forge (e.g. `https://gitlab.com`); the cluster base URL for Entire |
| `-token-file` | — | file holding the credential secret; `-` reads stdin (else `$ACCESS_TOKEN`) |
| `-user` | `x-access-token` | basic-auth username (token forges ignore it) |
| `-repos` / `-repo-pattern`+`-repo-count` | — | target repo path(s), appended verbatim; `-repo-pattern` expands `{n}` to `1..N` |
| `-strategy` | `branch` | `branch` \| `repo` \| `clone` \| `session` |
| `-branch-prefix` | — | prepended verbatim to branch names, before the run ID (e.g. `bench/` → `refs/heads/bench/fm...`); groups branches for easy cleanup |
| `-concurrency` | `1,8,32,128` | swept sequentially, one row each |
| `-duration` / `-warmup` | `60s` / `10s` | measured window / discarded ramp |
| `-files-min`/`-files-max`/`-file-size` | `1`/`10`/`2048` | commit shape; ignored by `clone` |
| `-object-format` | `auto` | `sha1` \| `sha256`; `auto` probes the Entire advertisement (generic/github default sha1) |
| `-session-commits` | `5` | session strategy checkpoints per cloned session |
| `-clone-depth`/`-base-ref` | `1`/default | clone/session strategy knobs |
| `-insecure` | `false` | skip TLS verification (dev / self-signed hosts) |
| `-out` | — | JSON results path (default `results/forgemark-<id>.json`) |

### Entire (supplying `-token-url` + `-jurisdiction` selects it)

| flag | notes |
|---|---|
| `-token-url` | core `/oauth/token` endpoint (presence selects Entire) |
| `-jurisdiction` | jurisdiction audience host, bare origin (presence selects Entire) |
| `-client-id` | public OAuth client id (default `entire-cli`) |

In this mode `-token-file`/`ACCESS_TOKEN` carries the subject token to exchange,
not a forge PAT.

## Environment variables

| var | notes |
|---|---|
| `ACCESS_TOKEN` | the credential secret, if `-token-file` isn't given: the forge token, or Entire's subject token. `-token-file` is preferred (keeps the secret out of the environment too). |

## How it works

- **Each agent** keeps an in-memory go-git repo (object format matched to the
  remote), commits 1–10 small files per iteration, and pushes its own branch in
  a tight loop. Agents are pinned round-robin across the target's nodes.
- **Clone runs** create each shallow clone in memory and discard it after
  recording latency, so the client side stays off disk.
- **Stats**: every operation is timed; warm-up samples are dropped; exact
  percentiles are computed from the sorted OK-latency set.

## Caveats

- Run the generator **close to the target** (same region). Push latency from a
  distant machine is dominated by round-trip time, so you'd be measuring the
  network path, not the forge. Watch the generator's CPU stays below 100% at the
  top concurrency level, or it — not the server — is your bottleneck.
- `branch`/`repo` leave one per-agent branch each on the target (no cleanup);
  `session` deletes each ephemeral branch as the agent abandons it; `clone`
  does not write refs. Use throwaway repos regardless. Pass `-branch-prefix`
  (e.g. `bench/`) to namespace the branches so they're easy to find and delete
  on the target afterwards.
- `branch`/`repo` use force-push on agent-owned refs so numbers aren't polluted
  by spurious non-fast-forwards; the server still does the full receive-pack, so
  throughput is unaffected.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## What landed

`forgemark report --emit monitor <results.json>` → the Entire runner `last_json_line` contract, peak sustained ops/sec as the value:

```
{"value":42.7,"rationale":"peak push 42.7 ops/s @ c=32 | c=1 8.1, c=8 28.4, c=32 42.7 | p95 210ms | 0 errors"}
```

Dead/empty target → `value: 0` (a gate reads it as a regression, not a pass). Reads legacy and format-2 docs. Branched off `main`, independent of the web-demo (#13) and threshold (#6) stacks, so it can land in any order.

## Where the plan stands now, corrected against the repo

- **Layer 1 (this repo, no Entire dep):** the monitor adapter is done (#14). The 5 runner JSONs already in `.entire/runners/` are the *reviewers* — you don't need to author perf-runner JSONs by hand yet; they belong with the runtime work.
- **Layer 2 (CI proof):** buildable today. A GitHub Actions job runs forgemark against a target, `report --emit monitor` emits the value, and PR #6's exit-2 threshold gate fails the PR. Zero new Entire infra. This is the cheapest next PR if you want a visible proof — but note #6 isn't merged yet, so it'd depend on #6 or duplicate its logic.
- **Layer 3 (native regional runner):** blocked on your three backend answers, and the repo now gives hard evidence for two of them: every runner here is `prompt_runner` with `repo_token: read` and a prompt that forbids network/load. So there is no exec/egress runtime today — forgemark genuinely justifies a new runner kind with egress + region pinning. That's the strategic headline and the real work.

Your three questions, still yours to confirm from the backend: (1) does a Gate threshold a `trail_monitor`, (2) is there any exec/command runner kind server-side, (3) can a sandbox get outbound git + regional placement. Layers 1 and 2 don't block on them; layer 3 is entirely gated by (2) and (3).

Want me to do **layer 2** next — a `.github/workflows/perf-gate.yml` that runs a demo/real target, emits the monitor, and gates via #6? If so, tell me whether to base it on #6's branch (so the flags exist) or keep it demo-only on `main` for now.

# Performance gate: run ForgeMark against a real forge and fail if peak
# throughput falls below a floor. This is the CI half of `forgemark report
# --emit monitor` — the run emits a monitor value and this workflow gates on it.
#
# It is intentionally NOT a pull_request trigger: a real git load test needs a
# credential and sustained egress to a forge, so it runs on demand
# (workflow_dispatch) or on a nightly schedule against secrets, never as a
# blocking check on every PR. GitHub-hosted runners have internet egress but no
# regional placement — see the "Caveats" note in the README about running close
# to the target for a faithful number.
#
# Required repository secrets for the live job:
#   FORGEMARK_REMOTE  base URL of the forge, e.g. https://gitlab.com
#   FORGEMARK_REPOS   comma-separated repo paths (must already exist), e.g. you/bench.git
#   FORGEMARK_TOKEN   forge access token (used as ACCESS_TOKEN, off argv)

name: Performance gate

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      concurrency:
        description: "concurrency sweep (comma-separated)"
        default: "1,8"
      duration:
        description: "measured window per level"
        default: "30s"
      min_push_rate:
        description: "fail if peak push/sec is below this"
        default: "1"
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * *" # 06:00 UTC nightly

jobs:
  # Proves the gate plumbing with zero secrets: build forgemark, reduce a sample
  # result doc to its monitor value, and assert the value-floor logic both ways.
  # This always runs, so the gate mechanism itself is covered even when the live
  # job below is skipped for want of secrets.
  gate-smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v2
        with:
          install: true
          cache: true
      - name: Build forgemark
        run: go build -o forgemark ./cmd/forgemark
      - name: Reduce sample result to a monitor value
        run: |
          ./forgemark report --emit monitor examples/sample-results.json | tee monitor.json
          value=$(jq -r '.value' monitor.json)
          echo "peak = $value push/s"
          # Gate logic: pass above the floor, fail below it. Verified both ways.
          awk -v v="$value" 'BEGIN { exit !(v >= 1) }' \
            || { echo "expected sample value >= 1"; exit 1; }
          awk -v v="$value" 'BEGIN { exit !(v < 9999) }' \
            || { echo "expected sample value < 9999"; exit 1; }

  # The real gate: load-test the target and fail the run if peak push/sec is
  # below the floor. Skips cleanly if the forge secrets aren't configured.
  perf:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v2
        with:
          install: true
          cache: true
      - name: Build forgemark
        run: go build -o forgemark ./cmd/forgemark
      - name: Check for forge secrets
        id: cfg
        env:
          REMOTE: ${{ secrets.FORGEMARK_REMOTE }}
          REPOS: ${{ secrets.FORGEMARK_REPOS }}
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGEMARK_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$REMOTE" ] || [ -z "$REPOS" ] || [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::FORGEMARK_REMOTE/REPOS/TOKEN not set — skipping the live perf gate."
          else
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Run benchmark
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.ready == 'true'
        env:
          ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FORGEMARK_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          ./forgemark \
            -remote "${{ secrets.FORGEMARK_REMOTE }}" \
            -repos "${{ secrets.FORGEMARK_REPOS }}" \
            -concurrency "${{ github.event.inputs.concurrency || '1,8' }}" \
            -duration "${{ github.event.inputs.duration || '30s' }}" \
            -out results/perf.json
      - name: Gate on peak throughput
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: |
          floor="${{ github.event.inputs.min_push_rate || '1' }}"
          ./forgemark report --emit monitor results/perf.json | tee monitor.json
          value=$(jq -r '.value' monitor.json)
          echo "peak = $value push/s (floor $floor)"
          awk -v v="$value" -v f="$floor" 'BEGIN { exit !(v >= f) }' || {
            echo "::error::peak push throughput $value/s is below the floor $floor/s"
            exit 1
          }
      - name: Upload result doc
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.ready == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: forgemark-perf-results
          path: results/perf.json

## Summary

Two halves of the same story: **emit a gateable number, then gate on it.**

1. **`forgemark report --emit monitor <results.json>`** reduces a stored result doc to one headline metric — **peak sustained ops/sec across the sweep** — in the Entire trail runner's `last_json_line` monitor contract:

   ```
   {"value":42.7,"rationale":"peak push 42.7 ops/s @ c=32 | c=1 8.1, c=8 28.4, c=32 42.7 | p95 210ms | 0 errors"}
   ```

2. **`.github/workflows/perf-gate.yml`** consumes that value: it runs forgemark against a real forge and fails when peak throughput drops below a floor.

### report

- `--emit monitor` (default) prints exactly the `{"value","rationale"}` object as the last JSON line of stdout. `--emit text` prints a human summary.
- `value` = peak OK ops/sec of the selected target (push side; clone/sec for `-strategy clone`, labeled accordingly).
- A target that **died or measured nothing reports `value: 0`**, so a gate reads it as a regression, not a silent pass.
- `-target <name>` selects among a multi-target comparison doc; default is the first target.
- Reads legacy format-1 and format-2 docs — `results.LoadPath` applies the same normalization `Load` does, with normalization now in one shared decoder.

### perf gate

- `workflow_dispatch` + nightly `schedule`, **not** `pull_request`: a live git load test needs a credential and sustained egress, so it runs on demand / on a schedule, never blocking every PR. GitHub-hosted runners have egress but no regional placement (see README caveat).
- Live job uses `FORGEMARK_REMOTE` / `FORGEMARK_REPOS` / `FORGEMARK_TOKEN` secrets and skips cleanly when they're absent.
- Gates purely on the monitor value (jq + a value floor), so it depends only on `report` here — it does **not** require the threshold flags in #6, though it composes with them.
- A secret-free `gate-smoke` job reduces `examples/sample-results.json` and asserts the floor logic both ways, covering the gate plumbing even when the live job skips.

## Testing

- `TestMonitorFor` (peak selection incl. a non-monotonic dip, clone labeling, dead/empty → 0, error summing), `TestSelectTarget`, `TestRound1`, `results.TestLoadPath`.
- Verified the report live against synthetic format-2, legacy format-1, clone, and dead-target docs; verified the workflow smoke steps (build → report → jq → awk floor) locally, both pass-above-floor and fail-below-floor. `go build`, `go test ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `golangci-lint`, and workflow YAML all clean.

5	ForgeMark measures **sustained push or clone throughput and per-operation
6	latency** the way an agent fleet hits a forge: many concurrent writers, readers,
7	or mixed sessions. It drives **real git operations** through
8	[`go-git`](https://github.com/go-git/go-git) (packfile build + ref update for
9	pushes, upload-pack for clones), so it exercises the forge paths directly — not
10	a synthetic HTTP approximation.
11	
12	It works against **any smart-HTTP git host** — GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket,
13	self-hosted, GitHub Enterprise Server, github.com, and
14	[Entire](https://github.com/entireio). There's no target flag: the forge is
15	inferred from `-remote` (and, for Entire, from the auth flags you supply).
16	
17	> **Only run ForgeMark against infrastructure you own or are explicitly
18	> authorized to load-test.** A tight push loop is abusive traffic to a host that
19	> hasn't agreed to it.
20	
21	## Install
22	
23	```bash
24	go install github.com/entireio/forgemark/cmd/forgemark@latest
25	```
26	
27	## Web GUI
28	
29	`forgemark serve` starts a local dashboard over the same engine: configure a
30	run in the browser, watch live per-second throughput / latency-percentile /
31	error charts while it executes, and benchmark **multiple forges side by side**
32	— every concurrency level starts simultaneously on all targets, so the overlay
33	is a fair comparison.
34	
35	```bash
36	forgemark serve            # http://127.0.0.1:8377
37	```
38	
39	- **Try it with no forge**: add a `demo://` target (e.g.
40	  `demo://fast?p50=60ms&spread=3&err=0.01&cap=400`) — a synthetic latency
41	  generator that exercises the whole pipeline offline. Add two with different
42	  profiles to see the comparison view.
43	- **Targets** take the same parameters as the CLI flags (remote, repos, object
44	  format, and the Entire fields). The credential is never typed into the
45	  browser: each target names a **source** — `gh CLI login` / `glab CLI login` /
46	  `entire CLI login` — and the server reads the token from that
47	  already-authenticated CLI at run start, so it never enters the page or the
48	  request body. (For GitLab the server uses glab's git-credential helper, which
49	  returns a repository-scoped token even when glab's stored API token isn't.)
50	  **Add from CLI logins** prefills complete GitHub / GitLab / Entire targets
51	  (endpoints, repos, credential source) from whichever CLIs you're logged into,
52	  and the **⚡ Push race preset** fills the race workload and opens the race
53	  view. A forge without a supported CLI login is benchmarked from the command
54	  line (`forgemark -token-file …`), not the web form.
55	- **History** lists every result doc in `results/` — CLI runs included — and
56	  overlays any selection as ops/s-vs-concurrency and p95-vs-concurrency curves.
57	  Server runs also store their 1-second live series, so finished runs replay.
58	- The server binds to loopback by default and refuses cross-origin requests.
59	  It is a load-generation control panel: the same authorization warning as the
60	  CLI applies, and starting a run requires confirming it in the form.
61	
62	`-addr` changes the listen address (a warning prints if it isn't loopback);
63	`-results` points at a different results directory.
64	
65	### Local comparison without pasting tokens
66	
67	Two scripts make the GitHub-vs-Entire comparison fully local — nobody shares or
68	pastes a token, ever:
69	
70	```bash
71	scripts/login.sh           # one-time: authenticate the gh and entire CLIs
72	scripts/compare-local.sh   # start (or reuse) the server and kick off a run
73	scripts/pushrace.sh        # demo mode: a 60s live head-to-head push race
74	```
75	
76	`pushrace.sh` presets a race-shaped workload — one flight of 16 agents pushing
77	checkpoint-sized commits (1-3 files × 1KB) at every target simultaneously for
78	one minute — and opens the GUI's **race view** (`#race/<run-id>`): a countdown,
79	one lane per forge, and a podium with the verdict when the flag drops. Three
80	metrics to race on (switchable live, or deep-linkable as
81	`#race/<run-id>/<metric>`):
82	
83	- **Throughput** — cumulative successful pushes; the leader fills the track.
84	- **Latency** — rolling 10s p50, lower wins; bar length is relative speed, so
85	  lower latency literally looks faster.
86	- **Reliability** — successful pushes ÷ attempts (errors and CAS rejections
87	  count as failures).
88	
89	Every number is measured, an exact tie is called a dead heat, and a caption
90	under the lanes — generated from the run's actual workload — states precisely
91	what is being watched: the commit shape, the loop, what the counters and
92	windows mean, and that client-side network round-trip is included. Any run can
93	be watched either way; the dashboard and race views link to each other.
94	
95	Mind what the Entire target measures: **mirror mode** (compare-local's
96	default) pushes through a GitHub mirror, which write-throughs to GitHub on
97	every push — that benchmarks the sync flow and can never beat GitHub itself.
98	**Native mode** (`FM_ENTIRE_NATIVE=1`, the pushrace default) auto-creates a
99	plain EntireDB repo (`et/forgemark-<you>/forgemark-target`) and benchmarks the
100	forge directly.
101	
102	[`scripts/compare-local.sh`](scripts/compare-local.sh) posts its targets with
103	a credential **source** (`secret_source: gh | entire`) instead of a token: the
104	server pulls each credential from your already-authenticated CLI at run start,
105	so no token ever passes through the script, the request body, or the browser.
106	Everything else is provisioned on first use:
107	
108	- a private throwaway GitHub repo (`<you>/forgemark-target`, seeded with an
109	  initial commit),
110	- its EntireDB mirror on your jurisdiction's default cluster
111	  (`entire repo mirror create` is idempotent, so re-runs are free),
112	- and `forgemark serve` itself, if nothing is listening.
113	
114	The Entire endpoints (token URL, jurisdiction audience, cluster) come from the
115	server's own discovery endpoint (`GET /api/local/suggest`, derived from your
116	active `entire auth` login context) — the same source the GUI's "Add from CLI
117	logins" button uses, so that logic exists once. Every repo, endpoint, and
118	workload knob is an `FM_*` environment variable — see the header comment in
119	the script; `FM_GITHUB_ONLY=1` skips the Entire target. Defaults keep
120	concurrency at `1,4` because of github.com's abuse limits (see below).
121	
122	## What it measures
123	
124	Per concurrency level it reports successful operations/sec,
125	p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max latency, and CAS-failure / error counts where they apply.
126	Results print as a table and are written to `results/forgemark-<id>.json` for
127	charting.
128	
129	### Strategies
130	
131	| `-strategy` | shape | what it tells you |
132	|---|---|---|
133	| `branch` (default) | N agents, **one repo**, each pushes its own branch | **Headline single-repo number.** No client-side contention (each agent owns its ref), so it isolates the server's per-repo ref-update path. |
134	| `repo` | N agents spread across **M repos** (`-repo-count`), own branches | Horizontal-scale ceiling — distinct repos serialize independently, so this should scale where `branch` saturates. |
135	| `clone` | N agents, **one repo**, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → discard → repeat | Read-side ceiling: how many concurrent shallow clones/sec the forge sustains, without write load. |
136	| `session` | N agents, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → commit+push `-session-commits` checkpoints to a fresh ephemeral branch → abandon → repeat | Realistic agent lifecycle: interleaves **read load (clone) with write load (push)** on one repo. Reports clone and push latencies separately. |
137	
138	## Usage
139	
140	Two steps: **set up the target repos**, then **run**.
141	
142	### 1. Set up targets
143	
144	ForgeMark does not create repos — it pushes to ones you provide. Create them on
145	your forge and make sure your credential can push:
146

131	func readSecret(tokenFile string) (string, error) {
132		if tokenFile != "" {
